source: User weekly syllabus; primary educational and language documentation

weeks.title: Orientation
objectives: Read the mission before starting. Learn the controls, Run, Step and Oracle hints.
A new wallet starts with 20 coins. Each hint costs 6 coins; first clears award the configured rewards once.
weeks.mechanic: Read the mission before starting. Learn the controls, Run, Step and Oracle hints.

points: Read the mission before starting. Learn the controls, Run, Step and Oracle hints.
A new wallet starts with 20 coins. Each hint costs 6 coins; first clears award the configured rewards once.
Stage 2 is guided interface practice; the main flowchart lesson is Week 2.

weeks.title: Flowcharting
objectives: Terminators mark start/end; rectangles perform processes; parallelograms represent input/output.
Decision diamonds choose labeled alternatives. Arrows specify order and loop-back paths.
weeks.mechanic: Terminators mark start/end; rectangles perform processes; parallelograms represent input/output.

points: Terminators mark start/end; rectangles perform processes; parallelograms represent input/output.
Decision diamonds choose labeled alternatives. Arrows specify order and loop-back paths.
Test both branches and boundary inputs before accepting a chart.
lesson.example: Start → Read n → n > 0? → Yes/No output → End

weeks.title: Algorithms
objectives: An algorithm specifies precise steps; a program expresses a procedure in a programming language.
Identify inputs, processing and outputs. Trace intermediate state and check termination.
weeks.mechanic: An algorithm specifies precise steps; a program expresses a procedure in a programming language.

points: An algorithm specifies precise steps; a program expresses a procedure in a programming language.
Identify inputs, processing and outputs. Trace intermediate state and check termination.
The register game is a small instruction language for algorithm practice, not C.

weeks.title: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
weeks.mission: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
objectives: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
weeks.mechanic: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.

lesson.summary: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
points: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
Portability needs care with implementation-dependent behavior. Middle-level is an informal classroom label, not an ISO language category.
lesson.example: C: Ritchie; Bell Labs; early 1970s; general purpose; procedural.

weeks.title: C Components, Keywords, Preprocessor and Organization
weeks.mission: C Components, Keywords, Preprocessor and Organization
objectives: int and return are keywords; main and printf are identifiers, not keywords.
Preprocessing precedes compilation. #include supplies header content; #define specifies token replacement.
weeks.mechanic: int and return are keywords; main and printf are identifiers, not keywords.
stages: Build and verify a source file

lesson.summary: C Components, Keywords, Preprocessor and Organization
points: int and return are keywords; main and printf are identifiers, not keywords.
Preprocessing precedes compilation. #include supplies header content; #define specifies token replacement.
Organize directives, a main definition, declarations, statements and braces. Source construction is checked separately from the factory analogy.
lesson.practice: Build and verify a source file

weeks.title: Creating Simple C Programs and Program Structure
weeks.mission: Creating Simple C Programs and Program Structure
objectives: A hosted program begins at main. Braces form its body; statements execute in order.
Construct a short program using declarations, initialization, assignment and printf.
weeks.mechanic: A hosted program begins at main. Braces form its body; statements execute in order.

lesson.summary: Creating Simple C Programs and Program Structure
points: A hosted program begins at main. Braces form its body; statements execute in order.
Construct a short program using declarations, initialization, assignment and printf.
Adventure movement functions are LogiCade helpers declared in logicade.h, not standard C library functions.

weeks.title: Basic Parts of C and Variable Declarations
weeks.mission: Basic Parts of C and Variable Declarations
objectives: A declaration pairs a type and name; initialization supplies a first value, and assignment changes it.
Practice int, float, double and char, with suitable printf formats.
weeks.mechanic: A declaration pairs a type and name; initialization supplies a first value, and assignment changes it.

lesson.summary: Basic Parts of C and Variable Declarations
points: A declaration pairs a type and name; initialization supplies a first value, and assignment changes it.
Practice int, float, double and char, with suitable printf formats.
Names are case sensitive. Do not read an uninitialized automatic local.

weeks.title: Local and Global Variables
objectives: File-scope variables are declared outside functions; block-scope locals are visible in their block.
An inner declaration can hide an outer name. Leaving its scope restores the outer declaration.
weeks.mechanic: File-scope variables are declared outside functions; block-scope locals are visible in their block.

points: File-scope variables are declared outside functions; block-scope locals are visible in their block.
An inner declaration can hide an outer name. Leaving its scope restores the outer declaration.
Scope differs from lifetime: ordinary automatic locals belong to a block execution; file-scope objects have static storage duration.

weeks.title: Examination Practice: Weeks 2–8
objectives: Stages cover every topic from Weeks 2–8 using its corresponding activity.
Apply flowcharts, algorithms, C history, source organization, declarations and scope.
weeks.mechanic: Stages cover every topic from Weeks 2–8 using its corresponding activity.

points: Stages cover every topic from Weeks 2–8 using its corresponding activity.
